# versionCompare

<link-summary>Compares two version strings numerically.</link-summary>

<web-summary>versionCompare() — Compares two version strings numerically. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/string</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function versionCompare(version1: string, version2: string): number;
```

Each dot-separated group is compared as a number, so `1.10` is above `1.2` — which a string comparison gets backwards. A missing group counts as zero, which makes `"2"` and `"2.0"` equal.

Both arguments must satisfy `isValidVersion`: digits and dots only, no pre-release suffix.

## Parameters

| Parameter  | Type     | Description         |
| :--------- | :------- | :------------------ |
| `version1` | `string` | The first version.  |
| `version2` | `string` | The second version. |

## Returns

`number` — `-1` when the first is lower, `0` when they are equal, `1` when the first is higher.

## Throws

| Exception   | Condition                                      |
| :---------- | :--------------------------------------------- |
| `TypeError` | either argument is not a valid version string. |

## Examples

### Comparing

```javascript
versionCompare("1.2.0", "1.10.0"); // => -1
versionCompare("2.0", "2"); // => 0
versionCompare("1.2.3", "1.2.3-beta"); // throws TypeError
```
